propositions: The caused_by auto-derivation mechanism (derive_caused_by) lacks a provenance marker to distinguish blame-derived edges from explicitly supplied ones, making measurement of accuracy impossible despite being a central question for metrics consumers

File-level git blame over impacted paths achieves only 43% agreement with recorded edges and 50% abstention on closed bugs with caused_by edges (n=88 population), with strong history drift as a confounder

Against independently proven origins (n=8), the deriver reproduced zero correct attributions and misattributed once confidently (moist-short-lionfish), naming the innocent producer—the dominant defect shapes (unmet obligation, carrier commit, omission) were predicted to be hard for blame and largely abstain as designed

The fail-closed mechanism is working as intended; the residual risk is confident-but-wrong cases where consumer-edited-last defects with innocent producers are blamed to the producer by file-majority heuristics that cannot observe defect shape
A provenance field (derived: blame | explicit) is needed to make the metric's confidence computable and enable weighted treatment of different edge sources by consumers and reviewers
